newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Acquisition, new product a boon to Borsodchem - ING.
newsitem.headline: Acquisition, new product a boon to Borsodchem - ING.

text.p: Hungarian chemicals firm Borsodchem could substantially boost 1997 sales with the launch of a new product and an acquisition, ING Barings said, maintaining a "buy" rating for Borsodchem stocks.

"The chemical factory is planning to launch a new product in 1997 which could yield approximately one billion to two billion forints this year," ING Barings said in the January issue of its 'Eastern Europe Monthly."

"In addition Borsodchem is planning to acquire a chemical company in one of the CEFTA countries this year, which could potentially result in additional sales revenues of eight billion to ten billion forints in 1997," it added.
Company officials were not immediately available for comment. However, last week a company official confirmed to Reuters that Borsodchem was negotiating.
"There aren't any agreements at the moment. Talks are continuing and we can probably release some information in mid-March," the official said last week.
CEFTA (Central European Free Trade Agreement) countries are Hungary, Poland, Czech Republic, Slovakia and Slovenia.
ING Barings said the new production line should be financed out of internal cash flow, while the acquisition would require external resources.
Borsodchem shares have been on the higher end of a recent rally on the Budapest Stock Exchange this year, surging to above 5,800 forints from 4,050 forints at the end of 1996.

Last week the stock's price received a fresh boost after the company's chief executive officer confirmed that they expected an 50 to 100 percent corporate tax relief for 1997, stemming from Hungary's tax regulations.
